pages.text: "To the mainland!" Dari hopped toward the dock with an empty bag on his back. Today he would ride the mail boat. Dad followed. "Everything packed?"
"Yes!" Dad shook the bag lightly. Empty! "Looks rather flat." Dari had thought only of the trip and forgotten to pack. "Can't we just go?"
Dad asked, "What if the sun's hot on the boat and you have no hat?" Dari imagined a hot head and dry throat. "I wouldn't like that..."
Dad sat before him and raised a flipper. "Packing isn't hard. Count what you need and put it in one by one." Dari tilted his head. "Count?"
Dad opened his bundle and lined up a hat, water bottle, and handkerchief. "These three will help us on the mainland." Dari pointed to each with a flipper and named it.
Dad held the bag open. "Count and put them in." In went the hat! "One, hat!" Dad counted along.
In went the water bottle. "Two!" In went the handkerchief. "Three!" Together they called, "Into the bag—ready!" The bag grew plump.
Kkiruk called from the roof, "A boat!" The mail boat puttered to the dock. Dari put on his full bag. "Nothing missing now!" He slapped his tail.
The boat's pelican driver unloaded a mail sack. "A well-packed bag! What's inside?" Dari tapped it. "One, hat! Two, water bottle! Three, handkerchief! Into the bag—ready!"
Aboard, Dad hugged Dari. "Our packing champion!" Counting one by one meant nothing was forgotten. Into the bag—ready! The mail boat set off for the mainland.
